default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-228.title: Dollar non-confirmation (SMT) extreme fade
E-228.hypothesis: Foreign flow buys the index and sells the dollar together, so a real WIN breakout to a new window high comes with WDO near its own window low; when WIN breaks out while WDO still sits in the upper part of its range, the break is local flow the macro side does not confirm, and dealers lean it back; fade (mirror).

E-229.title: Inside-higher-timeframe-candle micro-break fade
E-229.hypothesis: A short-term break that still closes inside the previous completed 15/30/60-minute candle is no break at all for the traders reading that higher timeframe: their resting orders and stops sit at that candle's high/low, not here, so the small breakout buyers get no follow-through and the move reverts; fade it.

E-230.title: Day-after-balanced-session micro-break fade
E-230.hypothesis: A session that closed almost where it opened (small body for its range) ended in balance: both sides accepted the range and nobody carried conviction overnight; the next session's participants trade responsively, so its short-term breaks lack an initiator and are faded.

E-231.title: Heavy-volume ceiling break fade
E-231.hypothesis: When the recent window's high was printed by a bar trading well above normal volume for its minute, a large seller showed size at that price; a later close just above it runs into that same participant's remaining offers rather than an empty book, so the break is absorbed and reverts (mirror at lows).

E-232.title: No-overnight-news day micro-break fade
E-232.hypothesis: A session opening almost at yesterday's close (gap small next to the 20-session typical gap) brought no overnight information to be priced, so no informed parent order is being worked during the day; intraday breaks are then local noise that liquidity providers fade.

E-233.title: Late MACD signal-cross fade
E-233.hypothesis: A MACD signal-line cross in the direction the MACD already sits (bullish cross above zero, bearish below) is a late, crowded retail trigger arriving after the move; the short-term traders who buy it are the liquidity the earlier movers exit into, so fade the cross.

E-234.title: Front-loaded-session micro-break fade
E-234.hypothesis: When the first hour took a larger share of the session's volume than usual for the time, the day's information was traded early and the rest of the session is digestion by responsive traders; later short-term breaks have no new initiator behind them, so fade them.

E-235.title: Off-peak-minute micro-break fade
E-235.hypothesis: At minutes whose seasonal volume (20-session median) sits well below the session average, the participants who carry information (institutional desks, foreign flow) are mostly absent; breaks then are small orders through quotes that market makers fade, regardless of whether liquidity is rising or falling.

E-236.title: Jump-free tape micro-break fade
E-236.hypothesis: When bipower variation explains all of the recent realized variance, the price moved by many small steps and no jump (no news, no forced burst): a diffusive, maker-dominated tape; a 10-minute break in that regime is one more random step that liquidity providers lean back on, so fade it.

E-237.title: Early-extreme side micro-break fade
E-237.hypothesis: The day's high or low is often set early; when the first hour made its high before its low, the early high is the extreme the morning sellers defend and the day's bias is down, so after the first hour short-term breaks upward toward it are faded (mirror when the low came first).
